title: Tourists Report Rise in Online Travel Scams
paragraphs: Booking a holiday online is convenient, but it also carries risks. According to recent research, a growing number of travelers are encountering scams when planning and booking their trips, and artificial intelligence is making these scams increasingly difficult to recognize.

In research published in May 2026, the cybersecurity company McAfee found that more than one in three Americans had encountered a travel-related scam or cyberthreat. Among those affected, 41% said they had lost money, and nearly half of this group lost more than $500. The most common methods used to trick victims included fake travel deals or promotions, false booking confirmations or travel updates, and misleading accommodation listings. Moreover, 69% of people surveyed said that AI-generated content makes travel scams harder to spot.

Rising travel costs appear to be part of the problem. According to McAfee, many travelers feel pressure to book quickly in order to secure a good price, which can lead them to make careless decisions. Scammers also frequently impersonate well-known travel brands. In fact, McAfee found that fake versions of the Tripadvisor app were created at about three times the rate of other major travel platforms.

A similar trend has been observed in the UK. In a survey by the research company Opinium, 34% of holidaymakers said they had seen more travel scams on social media over the past year, while 70% said they were wary of holiday promotional emails.

According to the cybersecurity company Bitdefender, common scams include fake rental listings that use stolen or AI-generated photos, fake flight deals, phishing emails that appear to come from airlines or hotels and messages on WhatsApp from people pretending to be hotel staff. Warning signs include pressure to act immediately, prices that seem too good to be true and requests to pay by bank transfer or outside the booking platform.

Experts advise travelers to book through official websites, research companies carefully and contact hotels using the phone numbers listed on their official sites. Anyone who becomes a victim should contact their bank immediately and report the incident.
